name: Private credit stress
value: Q3 exits ~10–11.5% of NAV vs 5% caps
summary: Non-traded BDC redemption requests far above 5% caps; backlog $8.2bn
state: In Q3, 19 non-traded BDCs received redemption requests worth 11.5% of NAV and met about 40%, leaving $8.2bn unmet (Stanger, via AltsWire). Blackstone's BCRED bought back $2.1bn in Q3 as requests held near 10% of shares. Requests eased from Q2, but gates remain in force; no new data as of 3 Nov.
for_you: Investors in semi-liquid private credit funds may not be able to withdraw money when they want; funds limit quarterly redemptions.

sources.title: AltsWire — BCRED buys back $2.1bn in Q3 as requests hold near 10%
AltsWire — Non-traded BDC redemption requests decrease in Q3

why: Private credit has grown fast outside bank regulation; its losses surface late and can spill into banks, insurers and pension funds.
drivers: Defaults among leveraged mid-sized borrowers, payment-in-kind interest, fund redemption requests, bank lending to funds.

rubric.alert: Several large funds gate at once, forced asset sales, or losses spreading to banks or insurers.
rubric.watch: A large fund limits redemptions, listed BDCs trade at wide discounts to NAV, or a cluster of borrower defaults with heavy losses.
rubric.normal: No notable fund gates, defaults or markdowns beyond the routine.
